answer:
RESULT (all four requested items executed; scripts re-run clean from scratch in ~10 s).

HYPOTHESIS (answer to the question). The gardening pathway switches its prevalence style along a land-use-intensity gradient, not along climate: gardening becomes the majority introduction style in warm, low-elevation coastal-plain habitats whose surrounding matrix is heterogeneous and only partly converted (Wetlands and Coastal: ~182 m, 14.6 °C, 645 mm, 22-26% urban and 17-26% cropland cover at 500 m), where it supplies 0.56 [0.42-0.69] and 0.54 [0.39-0.68] of invaded-plot occurrences at high absolute intensity (76 and 79 gardening occurrences per 100 plots); it drops to a minority style where a single intensive land use governs propagule pressure - Croplands (62% cropland at 50 m) 0.19 [0.12-0.27] and built-up Urban (69% urban at 50 m, closest to roads, the only habitat with net regressive land-cover change) 0.30 [0.23-0.37] - because unintentional contaminant introductions dominate there (0.77 and 0.69 of occurrences). Urban is a "high-intensity, low-share" style, not an absence of garden origin (69 gardening occurrences per 100 plots, second only to Coastal/Wetlands): its low share is compositional dilution by the largest unintentional influx recorded (163 per 100 plots). Riparian is a third style: intermediate gardening share (0.36 [0.27-0.46], statistically indistinguishable from the pooled mean, MC per-cell p=0.83) combined with a strong AgriForest concentration (13 of 23 AgriForest occurrences; standardised residual +3.93, MC p=0.0006), i.e. a legacy agro-silvopastoral signature along watercourses. Measured context depresses the gardening share both among and within habitats (urban 500 m OR 0.73 [0.59-0.91] per SD, p=0.005; cropland 500 m OR 0.73 [0.59-0.89], p=0.002; within-habitat urban -0.29 logit per SD, p=0.018), and the joint mosaic is clearly ordered: share 0.448 where urban<=0.15 and cropland<=0.15 vs 0.245 where both exceed 0.15. By contrast elevation, rainfall, distance to stream/road and 1993-2009 landscape change contribute nothing once habitat is accounted for. Since habitat labels still improve fit beyond all measured context (quasi-F=7.01, p=5e-06) while context barely improves on habitat labels (quasi-F=1.67, p=0.12; beta-binomial 2dlogL=9.54, 3 df, p=0.023), the unexplained part is attributed to unmeasured proximity to the propagule source (gardens, nurseries, ornamental plantings) rather than to abiotic context. Context framing only: the gardening share of the regional introduction flux rose from 0.168 before 1500 to 0.752 in 1985-2019 (chi2=230.4, p=6e-47), so habitat differences reflect where this dominant flux establishes, not its size.

a) PLOT-LEVEL MODELS. Primary quasi-binomial (successes=n.gard, trials=n.total, AgriForest folded, invaded plots n=191/481 occurrences, 6 classes): dispersion phi=1.01, deviance 231.8/185 (null 268.6), deviance explained 13.7%, LRT=36.7, df=5, quasi-F=7.28, p=3.0e-06. Beta-binomial converged: overdispersion rho=0.0177, LRT=35.33, df=5, p=1.3e-06 (i.e. little extra-binomial noise at plot level). Habitat means with intervals (beta-binomial): Wetlands 0.564 [0.421-0.697], Seminatural-pooled 0.552 [0.375-0.717], Coastal 0.535 [0.384-0.680], Riparian 0.368 [0.274-0.473], Urban 0.297 [0.228-0.377], Croplands 0.187 [0.123-0.273]. ORs vs Croplands: Wetlands 5.55 [3.20-9.63], Seminatural-pooled 5.34 [2.80-10.20], Coastal 5.06 [2.83-9.05], Riparian 2.52 [1.56-4.09], Urban 1.87 [1.19-2.93]. Unpooled 10-level model: phi=0.98, deviance explained 18.9%, quasi-F=5.73, p=5.5e-07, but Broad-leaved (4 occurrences) and Rock outcrops (1) show quasi-complete separation (estimates +/-21-24, SE~1e4) - descriptive only. Sensitivity 1 (all-plots denominator, 632 plots): phi=1.01, deviance explained 22.9%, quasi-F=27.46, p=1.1e-16; Sensitivity 2 (AgriForest dropped, 396 occurrences): quasi-F=6.71, p=1.0e-05, all ORs unchanged (5.23, 5.70, 2.28, 1.70).

b) PERMUTATION / MONTE-CARLO G-TESTS (B=20000). 6 classes x 3 pathways: G=56.14, df=10, MC p=5e-05 (4/18 expected cells<5); 6 classes gardening vs non-gardening: G=36.74, df=5, MC p=5e-05, 0/12 cells<5; unpooled 10 x 3: G=77.22, df=18, MC p=5e-05 (17/30 cells<5, hence MC required). Plot-level permutation of pathway counts across plots: G=36.74 (6 classes) and 50.62 (10 habitats), both MC p=5e-05. Driving cells (residual, MC two-sided p; Bonferroni 0.0028): Croplands gardening -2.91 (0.0004), Wetlands gardening +2.51 (0.0023), Coastal gardening +2.03 (0.017), Seminatural-pooled gardening +1.85 (0.024), Urban unintentional +1.39 (0.031), Riparian AgriForest +3.93 (0.0006).

c) CONTEXT OF STAND-OUTS. Gardening-dominant (Wetlands+Coastal): 182 m, 14.63 °C, 645 mm, urban 0.128 (50 m) / 0.240 (500 m), cropland 0.135 / 0.218, 736 m from road, landscape change 1993-2009 +0.04. Low-style: Croplands 415 m, 13.56 °C, 682 mm, urban 0.063 / 0.133, cropland 0.621 / 0.445, 550 m from road; Urban 197 m, 14.75 °C, 657 mm, urban 0.689 / 0.566, cropland 0.093 / 0.126, 467 m from road, change -0.077. So high gardening prevalence sits in warm, low, moist coastal-plain habitats with mixed low-to-moderate cover; low prevalence sits in habitats under a single dominant intensive cover (cropland or dense urban fabric). Kept one variable per collinear pair (urban500 over 1000 r=0.95, cropland500 over 1000 r=0.93, elevation over temperature r=-0.96); radiation dropped.

d) CONTEXT-EXPLANATION MODELS. Context only (7 variables, no habitat labels): 4.5% deviance explained, quasi-F=1.57, p=0.147; urban500_z OR/SD 0.732 [0.588-0.911] p=0.005, cropland500_z 0.727 [0.592-0.892] p=0.002, elevation/rainfall/change/distances n.s. Habitat+context: 18.3% deviance explained, quasi-F=3.89, p=2.7e-05, urban remains negative (-0.289, p=0.024). Within-habitat (5 informative habitats with habitat fixed effects): urban500_z -0.293 (p=0.018) and elevation_z +0.269 (p=0.025); the same covariates pooled without habitat terms are non-significant overall (quasi-F=1.43, p=0.226), i.e. context is a within-habitat modifier while the habitat labels carry most signal. Built/cultivated vs wet-seminatural contrast: OR 0.380 [0.285-0.507], p=1.8e-06. Leave-one-habitat-out (all five informative) leaves every contrast unchanged to 2 d.p.; leave-one-5km-cell-out over the 8 richest cells keeps the WetCoastal OR in 2.43-3.01.

FLAGGED (not hidden). (1) The apparent gardening richness of the pooled remote seminatural class is NOT robust: invaded-plot share 0.55 (OR 5.34) reverses to OR 0.15 (p<0.001) under the all-plots denominator, because only 17/347 of its plots are invaded (4.9 gardening occurrences per 100 plots vs 69.2 in Urban). Coniferous 0.88 (n=8), Broad-leaved 1.00 (n=4), Scrublands 0.40 (n=5), Rock outcrops 0.00 (n=1) are uninformative individually. (2) Riparian's signal is AgriForest concentration, not gardening. (3) Species non-independence is not modelled (481 occurrences from ~77 species, no plot-species crosswalk); phi=0.98-1.10 and rho=0.018 limit but do not remove this caveat. (4) Cropland cover is non-monotone at the extreme (>60% cropland share 0.375; quadratic p=0.018), so the cultivation gradient is best described as a mid-range decline. (5) Species-level niche-breadth commentary (gardening median 0.377 vs unintentional 0.835, Mann-Whitney p=0.0147) comes from a file with no crosswalk to plots and is used only as mechanism commentary; no phylogenetic modelling was performed.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway shows different prevalence styles according to the intensity and heterogeneity of the surrounding land use, not according to climate. In warm, low-elevation, humid coastal-plain habitats with a heterogeneous, only partly converted matrix (Wetlands and Coastal: ~182 m, 14.6 °C, 645 mm, 22-26% urban and 17-26% cropland cover at 500 m), gardening is the dominant style, supplying the majority of established non-native occurrences (0.56 [0.42-0.69] and 0.54 [0.39-0.68]) at the highest absolute intensity recorded (76-79 gardening occurrences per 100 plots). In habitats governed by a single intensive land use the gardening style is diluted by unintentional contaminant introductions: Croplands (62% cropland at 50 m) falls to 0.19 [0.12-0.27] with 77% unintentional, and the built-up Urban habitat to 0.30 [0.23-0.37] with 69% unintentional - although Urban still receives high absolute gardening propagule input (69 occurrences per 100 plots), so its low share is compositional dilution rather than absence of garden-origin species. Riparian constitutes a third style: intermediate gardening share (0.36 [0.27-0.46], not different from the pooled mean) plus a strong concentration of the AgriForest pathway (13 of 23 occurrences, standardised residual +3.93, MC p=0.0006), i.e. a legacy agro-silvopastoral signature along watercourses. Measured context acts as a modifier in the same direction at both scales - each SD more urban cover reduces the gardening odds by ~27% among habitats (p=0.005) and by ~26% within habitats (p=0.018), cropland cover similarly (p=0.002), and plots with both urban and cropland cover above 15% have a gardening share of 0.245 versus 0.448 where both are below - whereas elevation, rainfall, distance to roads/streams and post-1993 landscape change add nothing once habitat is accounted for. Because habitat labels still improve fit beyond all measured context (quasi-F=7.01, p=5e-06) while context adds only marginally beyond habitat (p=0.12), we hypothesise that the residual differences reflect proximity to the ornamental propagule source (gardens, nurseries, plantings) interacting with habitat, rather than abional conditions: gardening-derived invasion becomes the dominant style in thermally benign, low-lying, structurally open wet/coastal habitats embedded in a mixed low-intensity matrix, and a minority style wherever cropland or dense urban fabric concentrates contaminant propagule pressure. All shares are shares of plot occurrences (plot-level unit), and the apparent gardening excess of the pooled remote seminatural habitats is a denominator artifact (OR 5.34 under invaded-plot denominator vs 0.15 under all-plots denominator) rather than an ecological signal.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspection (analysis/01_inspection.py): shapes, categorical levels, missingness, duplicate flags; established that invaded_niche_pathways.csv is one row per plot (632 unique coordinates, 0 NAs), that n.total == n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo, and that habitat totals are plot-weighted species occurrences (481 occurrences) rather than species richness; confirmed no crosswalk between the plot file and the 81-species trait file. 2) Data setup (analysis/02_main_analysis.py): success=n.gard, trials=n.total (AgriForest folded into non-gardening); primary frame = 191 invaded plots; sensitivities = all-plots denominator (any plot hosting >=1 gardening species, 632 plots) and AgriForest dropped (n.gard vs n.unint, 396 occurrences); all 10 habitats kept descriptively, five habitats with <=13 occurrences pooled into 'Seminatural-pooled' for confirmatory inference; Clopper-Pearson intervals for shares. 3) Models: quasi-binomial GLM on grouped binomial endog (statsmodels GLM, scale='X2', t-tests) for habitat-only, unpooled 10-level, both sensitivities, context-only, context+habitat, within-habitat (habitat fixed effects), 3-group contrasts, leave-one-habitat-out and leave-one-5km-cell-out refits; home-likelihood beta-binomial MLE (scipy, numerical Hessian SEs) for habitat means, context model and nested comparisons. 4) Permutation inference: Monte-Carlo multinomial G-test (B=20000, fixed row totals and pooled column proportions) on 10x3, 6x3 and 6x2 tables with simulated standardised residuals and per-cell two-sided MC p-values against a Bonferroni threshold, plus a plot-level permutation test in which pathway counts are shuffled across plots (habitat occurrence totals not held fixed). 5) Context characterisation: per-habitat means of elevation, temperature, rainfall, urban and cropland cover at 50 m and 500 m, distance to road/stream, progressive-minus-regressive landscape change, with one variable retained per collinear pair; two-axis style table (composition share vs occurrences per 100 plots); urban and cropland binned shares and a 2x2 cover mosaic; quadratic-term tests for monotonicity. 6) Robustness flagging and exports (results_*.csv, FINDINGS.md). 7) Temporal contingency table used only as one-sentence framing (no habitat key); phylogenetic tree not used (no phylogenetic modelling, per instructions).
